name: Ant (black garden ant)
headline: length
subtitle: Worker of the black garden ant, Lasius niger
description: The black garden ant is a small brown-black ant and one of the most familiar ants in European gardens. Its workers, the non-reproductive females seen foraging for most of the year, are about 3.4 to 5 mm long. Winged queens are roughly twice that size, and a colony has a single queen with anywhere from a few hundred to thousands of workers.

facts.text: Winged queens are almost twice the size of the workers.
A colony has a single queen and from several hundred up to 10,000 workers.
What was long called the common black ant is actually two separate species, Lasius niger and Lasius platythorax, first told apart in 1991.
The ants seen outside the nest for most of the year are female workers gathering food; large nests can hold more than 20,000 workers.

caveats: No university or museum page giving a Lasius niger worker body length could be fetched (AntWiki was blocked by a bot check, the BWARS species account gives no size, and a 2020 body-size study measured only head width). The worker, queen and male lengths come from NatureSpot, a UK biological recording site.

The Natural History Museum says queens 'can be up to 15 millimetres long', well above NatureSpot's 8 to 9 mm. The NHM article does not say how that length was measured, so it is not used as a measure.
No source with an ant's body mass was found.
